extracted.intended_audience: broadband internet service providers and other entities participating in the FCC Broadband Data Collection (including challengers, state/local/Tribal governments, and consumers)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and data quality requirements for filings to the FCC Broadband Data Collection (including Fabric and coverage maps), plus procedures for crowdsourcing, challenges, verification, confidentiality, and certifications. Applies to fixed, fixed wireless, mobile, and satellite broadband providers and challengers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shapefile (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A digital storage format containing geospatial or location-based data and attribute information regarding the availability of broadband internet access service and that can be viewed, edited, and mapped in geographic information system software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard broadband installation (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The initiation by a provider of fixed broadband internet access service in an area in which the provider has not previously offered that service, with no charges or delays attributable to the extension of the network of the provider, and includes the initiation of fixed broadband internet access service through routine installation that can be completed not later than 10 business days after the date on which the service request is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: H3 standardized geospatial indexing system (definition/use)
rubrics_metrics.description: A system overlaying Earth with hexagonal cells at various resolutions (hex-0 to hex-15) using a nested parent/child structure (each parent contains ~7 children); used for sampling and reporting (e.g., verification using H3 at resolution 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the geospatial indexing system and specific resolution references used in verification and sampling (e.g., resolution 8 for verification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entities required to file FCC Form 477
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities-based providers of broadband service; providers of local telephone service; facilities-based providers of mobile telephony service; and providers of Interconnected VoIP service to end users must file a completed FCC Form 477.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filings must follow Commission rules and instructions to Form 477.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification requirement for Form 477 filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each report must include a certification signed by an appropriate official of the respondent and shall report the title of their certifying official (as specified in Form 477 instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality: emergency operations and PII
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency operations contact information and personally identifiable information are information that should not be routinely available for public inspection pursuant to § 0.457 and related provisions; the Commission will withhold such data from public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider-specific subscription information confidentiality request
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents may request that provider-specific subscription information in FCC Form 477 filings be treated as confidential by indicating so on Form 477 at submission time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other data may be requested confidential with a separate request pursuant to § 0.459.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information the Commission will publicly release from Form 477
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will release provider-specific mobile deployment data; data regarding minimum advertised or expected speed for mobile broadband services; and location information necessary to permit accurate broadband mapping, including crowdsourcing/challenge processes. Providers may not request confidential treatment for these items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission decision authority on non-disclosure and limited sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission makes all non-disclosure decisions, but certain Bureau Chiefs may release provider-specific information to state commissions with protections, to 'eligible entities' in aggregated form under confidentiality conditions, or to others if access addresses competitive sensitivity and precludes public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file revised Form 477 for significant errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents shall file a revised version of FCC Form 477 if they discover a significant error. For counts, a difference amounting to 5 percent of the filed number is considered significant; for percentages, a difference of 5 percentage points is significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement for failure to file Form 477 correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file Form 477 in accordance with Commission rules and instructions may lead to enforcement action under the Act and other applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report frequency for Form 477 and Broadband Data Collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities subject to § 1.7001 must file reports semi-annually: on or before March 1 (data as of Dec 31 prior year) and September 1 (data as of June 30 current year). New entities must file for the reporting period in which they become eligible and semi-annually thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to update Form 477 content
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated Bureaus and Offices (Office of International Affairs, Space Bureau, Wireless Telecommunications Bureau, Wireline Competition Bureau, Office of Economics and Analytics) may update the specific content of data to be submitted on FCC Form 477 to reflect changes in technologies, GIS, and other related matters, and may implement technical improvements or clarifications to forms/filing mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of Broadband Data Collection filings
rubrics_metrics.description: All providers shall make biannual filings in the Broadband Data Collection portal and include data relating to availability and quality of service in accordance with the subpart. Terrestrial fixed or satellite providers must submit polygon shapefiles or list of addresses; fixed wireless must submit propagation maps and model details or list of addresses; submissions must include details of how the data were generated; fixed providers shall indicate whether reported service is available to residential and/or business customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting maximum advertised download/upload speeds (fixed providers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each provider of fixed broadband shall report the maximum advertised download and upload speeds associated with its service in an area. For services below 25 Mbps down/3 Mbps up, providers must use two speed tiers: (a) >200 kbps in at least one direction and <10 Mbps down/1 Mbps up; and (b) >=10 Mbps down/1 Mbps up and <25 Mbps down/3 Mbps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latency reporting requirement (fixed providers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed broadband providers shall indicate whether the network round-trip latency associated with each maximum speed combination in a geographic area is less than or equal to 100 milliseconds, based on the 95th percentile of measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum reporting distances for certain terrestrial fixed technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Terrestrial fixed providers using certain wireline technologies may not report coverage beyond defined maximum distances: DSL — not exceed 6,600 route feet from the DSL access multiplexer to customer premises for speeds >=25/3; FTTP — not exceed 196,000 route feet from optical line termination to optical network termination; HFC — not exceed 12,000 route feet from aggregation point to customer premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions allow reporting beyond maxima if provider has a current subscriber beyond bounds, previously had a subscriber, received universal service or other obligations and begun service, or received a waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed wireless propagation map modeling parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed wireless providers submitting coverage maps must base propagation maps/model details on: a cell edge probability of not less than 75% of receiving maximum advertised speeds; a cell loading factor of not less than 50%; and receiver heights within four to seven meters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed wireless required documentation and model validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed wireless providers must provide: name/version/developer of radio network planning tool(s); granularity of the model (e.g., 3-arc-second points); affirmation that the coverage model has been validated and calibrated at least once using on-the-ground testing or other real-world measurements by provider or vendor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed wireless base station and terrain/clutter disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers must disclose base station info (frequency bands, carrier aggregation usage, radio technologies per band, elevation, geographic coordinates) and terrain/clutter information (dataset name/vintage, clutter resolution, list and descriptions of clutter categories, link budget and description of other parameters including predicted signal strength).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also disclose height and power values used for receivers/CPE antennas in modeling (height 4–7 meters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile coverage map minimum service-speed parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile providers must submit coverage maps reflecting minimum expected user speeds at the cell edge: 3G — 200 kbps down / 50 kbps up; 4G LTE — 5 Mbps down / 1 Mbps up; 5G-NR — (a) minimum expected 7 Mbps down / 1 Mbps up and (b) minimum expected 35 Mbps down / 3 Mbps up at the cell edge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile coverage probability and cell-loading requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each mobile technology (3G, 4G LTE, 5G-NR) and for mobile voice services, provider coverage maps must reflect areas where users should expect to receive the minimum required speeds with a cell edge coverage probability of not less than 90% and a cell loading of not less than 50%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terrain/clutter and resolution requirements for mobile maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile coverage maps must account for terrain and clutter using terrain and clutter data with a resolution of 100 meters or better, and each coverage map must have a resolution of 100 meters or better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps must be submitted in vector format.

rubrics_metrics.name: RSRP/RSSI signal-level map requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each 4G LTE or 5G-NR propagation map, providers must also submit a second set of maps showing Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP) in dBm as measured at 1.5 meters AGL from each active cell site. For 3G propagation maps, a second set showing Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) is required only where 3G is the only technology offered. RSSI/RSRP values should be provided in 10 dB increments or finer beginning with −50 dBm and continuing to −120 dBm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile radio network planning tools disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile providers must disclose: tool name; version used to produce map; developer name; affirmation that model validated/calibrated at least once using drive tests/real-world measurements (with brief summary and date); the propagation model(s) used and brief descriptions if multiple; and model granularity (e.g., 3-arc-second points, bin sizes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propagation maps must depict outdoor coverage including use cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Propagation maps submitted must depict outdoor coverage including both on-street/pedestrian stationary usage and in-vehicle mobile usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link-budget disclosure and completeness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile providers must disclose all applicable link budgets and all parameters/parameter values used to design networks and provide service at defined speeds, including a description of how link budgets were developed and the rationale for specific values; the name/vintage/resolution of terrain and clutter datasets used; list of clutter categories and description of propagation loss due to clutter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must submit reasonable parameter values and propagation models consistent with how they model services when designing networks and may not omit link budget parameters or fail to account for constraints on coverage projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification requirements for Broadband Data Collection filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each filing must include a corporate officer certification that the officer has examined the submission and that, to the best of the officer's actual knowledge, all statements of fact are true and correct. Providers must also submit a certification of accuracy by a qualified engineer stating direct knowledge/responsibility for generation of the filing and that statements are true and correct and in accordance with the provider's ordinary course of network design and engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a corporate officer is also an engineer with requisite knowledge, a single certification may fulfill both requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified engineer definition for certification
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'qualified engineer' is: (1) a corporate officer with a Bachelor of Science in engineering and direct knowledge/responsibility for network design/construction; or (2) an engineer with a bachelor's or postgraduate degree in EE, electronic technology, or similar and at least 7 years relevant experience in broadband network design/performance; or (3) an employee/agent with specialized training relevant to broadband engineering/design/deployment/performance and at least 10 years relevant experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data protections and public release in Fabric and Broadband Data Collection filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will protect security, privacy, and confidentiality of non-public/competitively sensitive information in the Fabric and related datasets by withholding data required confidential pursuant to § 0.457 and all PII; subject to contractual/license restrictions, the Commission will make public other information about broadband availability at specific locations (e.g., coordinates, street addresses, whether a provider reported availability, and whether a dispute exists). Providers may request confidentiality for provider-specific subscription information at time of filing; other confidentiality requests must follow § 0.459.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audits of Broadband Data Collection filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Economics and Analytics, in coordination with relevant Bureaus, shall conduct regular audits of information submitted by providers. Audits may be random or required in cases of patterns of incorrect filings, as determined by the Office of Economics and Analytics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowdsourcing process and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities or individuals may submit crowdsourced data via the Commission's online portal to verify/supplement provider submissions. Crowdsourced filers must provide contact information; location (street address and/or coordinates); provider name; relevant details disputing deployment/availability; and a certification that, to the best of the filer's actual knowledge, all statements are true and correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-the-ground crowdsourced data must include metrics and meet testing parameters (except may include any combo of download/upload rather than both). The portal notifies providers but providers are not required to respond. Crowdsourced info will be made public except PII and information required confidential under § 0.457.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger for verification inquiry from crowdsourcing/other data
rubrics_metrics.description: If crowdsourced data and/or other available data lead the Commission to determine a provider's coverage info is likely inaccurate, the provider shall be subject to a verification inquiry consistent with the mobile verification process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile service verification: submission types and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile providers must submit either infrastructure information or on-the-ground test data in response to a Commission staff request to verify accuracy of propagation models/maps. Providers must submit data within 60 days of receiving the request. The Office of Economics and Analytics and Wireless Telecommunications Bureau may require additional data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical sampling and H3 resolution for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: On-the-ground verification must use a statistically appropriate sample for the area tested and verify coverage of a sampled area using the H3 geospatial indexing system at resolution 8. On-the-ground tests will be evaluated to confirm, using a one-sided 95% statistical confidence interval, that the cell coverage is 90% or higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-ground test frequency and spacing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A provider must record at least two tests within each randomly selected hexagon, with test times at least four hours apart (irrespective of date), unless the provider submits actual cell loading data for the cell(s) covering the hexagon sufficient to establish that median loading did not exceed modeled loading for the one-week period prior to the inquiry, in which case only a single test is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests within sampled hex that are outside the coverage area are treated as valid if no tests recorded within the coverage area. Slight GPS error may be accepted. Missing required tests are set as negative tests for final adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-vehicle mobile test rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For in-vehicle mobile tests, providers must conduct tests with the antenna located inside the vehicle.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-ground test length, averaging, and timing parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: On-the-ground tests must have minimum test length of 5 seconds and maximum of 30 seconds for each of download, upload, and latency measurements (not including ramp up time); test results must be reported averaged over test duration (total bits / total test time); tests must be conducted outdoors between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. local time. The minimum duration requirement is relaxed once a download or upload measurement has transferred at least 1,000 megabytes of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required metrics for each on-the-ground test
rubrics_metrics.description: Each test must include: testing app name/version; timestamp and duration of each metric; geographic coordinates (start and end) with GPS accuracy and location accuracy; consumer-grade device type/brand/model/OS; name/identity of provider tested; location of test server (hostname or IP); signal strength/quality/unique identifier/radiofrequency metrics of serving cell where available; download speed; upload speed; round-trip latency; whether test was in-vehicle or outdoor pedestrian stationary; vehicle speed for in-vehicle tests where available; indication if test failed to establish connection; network technology and spectrum bands used; and all other metrics required per the most recent specification adopted by OEA and WTB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure data required for verification inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting infrastructure data for verification, providers must include for each cell site: latitude/longitude; cell and site ID; ground elevation AMSL (meters); frequency bands including channel bandwidth; radio technologies used per band; backhaul capacity and type; number of sectors; EIRP (dBm) of sector at time of map creation; geographic coordinates of transmitters; per-site classification (urban/suburban/rural); antenna elevation above ground and specifications (make/model, beamwidth, radiation pattern, orientation/azimuth and electrical/mechanical down-tilt); operating transmit power; throughput and required signal strength and SNR; cell loading distribution; areas enabled with carrier aggregation and list of band combinations; and any additional parameters listed in the most-recent wireless infrastructure data specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed service challenge process required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Challengers (state/local/Tribal govts, consumers, others) may submit data to challenge coverage maps, provider-submitted availability info, or the Fabric. Challengers must provide: name/contact; street address or coordinates of disputed location(s); provider name; category of dispute (from portal options); for consumers evidence/details of a service request or evidence showing no availability (screenshots, emails); for governments/entities evidence including methodology, basis for determinations, communications with provider and outcome; for Fabric disputes, details/evidence about disputed location; representation that challenger resides/does business or is authorized to request service; and a certification that all statements are true and correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider notification and response timeline for availability/coverage challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Portal shall alert provider if a challenge with required elements is submitted. Within 60 days of alert, provider must: (i) accept allegations, in which case submit correction for challenged location within 30 days of reply; or (ii) deny allegations and provide evidence in portal and to challenger that provider serves (or could/will serve) the challenged location. If provider denies, provider and challenger have 60 days after provider's reply to attempt resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond within applicable timeframes results in a finding against provider and mandatory corrections to provider's Broadband Data Collection info within 30 days, or Commission will make corrections itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public designation and resolution timeline for challenged locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a complete challenge is submitted, the location is designated on coverage maps as 'in dispute/pending resolution.' If parties can't reach consensus within 60 days after provider's reply, the provider shall report status of efforts; Commission then has 90 days to review evidence and determine either in favor of challenger (provider updates info within 30 days of decision) or in favor of provider (location removed from 'in dispute').

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of proof for challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: In consumer challenges to availability and coverage map data, the consumer must make an initial showing by a preponderance of the evidence that provider data are inaccurate; the provider must then provide evidence by a preponderance of the evidence that its reported data are accurate. In challenges by governmental or other entities, the challenger must make a detailed, clear and methodologically sound showing by clear and convincing evidence that provider data are inaccurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabric challenge procedure differences
rubrics_metrics.description: For Fabric challenges, after a challenge with required information is filed the provider will receive a notice and can respond in the portal but is not required to do so; the Commission seeks to resolve such challenges within 60 days of receiving the challenge filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-location challenges allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Government entities or other entities may file challenges at multiple locations in a single challenge, but each challenged location must contain all required elements set forth for a single challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of challenge information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will make public information about the location subject to the challenge (including street address and/or coordinates), the name of the provider, and any relevant details concerning the basis for the challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile service consumer challenge: required contact and test-device info
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers submitting mobile coverage challenges must provide name, email address, and mobile phone number of the device on which the speed test was conducted. Speed test data must use a speed test app designated by the Office of Engineering and Technology (in consultation with OEA and WTB) for use in the challenge process.
